sentences.text: America once had two Thanksgivings, and every family had to pick one.
In nineteen thirty-nine, November had five Thursdays, so Thanksgiving fell on the very last day.
Shops panicked, because that meant fewer days to sell Christmas presents.
So President Roosevelt moved it a week earlier, and about half the states refused.
If your parents lived in one state and your in-laws in the next, you got two turkeys, or one fight.
Texas just took both days off.
It took Congress two years to lock in the fourth Thursday you'll eat on this week.
The shops picked your turkey's date.
Fair, or a step too far?
